stem: A healthcare operations study measures the wait time (minutes) for a sample of 15 emergency room visitors. The sample mean is 35.7 min with a sample standard deviation of 17.8 min. However, 3 of the 15 observations appear to be outliers (values more than 2.5 standard deviations from the mean). If these outliers are removed, the remaining 12 observations have a mean of 34.5 min and standard deviation of 11.2 min. Estimate the true population mean and provide a 95% confidence interval that accounts for the uncertainty about whether outliers should be included.

ground_truth.answer: With all data: mean = 35.7, 95% CI = [25.8, 45.6]. Without outliers: mean = 34.5, 95% CI = [28.0, 41.0]. Combined interval accounting for analytic uncertainty: [25.8, 45.6]. Point estimate: 35.1 min.

solution_steps: The outlier treatment choice creates structural uncertainty. Combined interval: [25.8, 45.6].
common_failure_modes: Using only the full sample without considering outlier impact
Removing outliers without reporting both analyses
Not recognizing that the choice of analysis method is itself a source of uncertainty
